selection: ADVERSARIAL, not representative. All 4 rows firing both instruments, both coverage-1.00 reproductions, and the 13 shortest rows in the census. If the style cannot carry these it cannot carry the corpus.
template: security-control :: An answer to a risk the organization chose not to accept; judged by whether the risk moved, not by whether the control is present.
test: A candidate who reads it knows something the ISO definition does not tell them: what the thing is FOR, when it applies, or what it is contrasted AGAINST.

rows.why_selected: both instruments; coverage 1.00 - the whole description is ISO/IEC 27000 cl.3
rows.proposed: The stage that produces the list everything later works from, so a risk missed here is never analysed, never treated, and invisible to anyone reviewing the register afterwards.

rows.why_selected: coverage 1.00 - the description IS the standard's title. Exempt from the leak gate as title class, which does not make it teach.
rows.current: guidance on information security risk management
rows.proposed: What you reach for when 27001 requires risk assessment but does not say how to do one. It offers method and examples, and no organization is ever audited against it.

rows.current: a potential cause of an unwanted incident
rows.proposed: The actor or event that could cause harm, named separately from the weakness it would need. Pairing the two is what turns a vague worry into something that can be assessed.

rows.current: the terms of reference against which risk significance is judged
rows.proposed: Fixed before assessment begins, never after the results arrive. Deciding what counts as acceptable once you can see which risks would fail it is how a register gets tuned to a wanted answer.

rows.current: information is accessible and usable on demand by an authorized entity
rows.proposed: The property that fails with no attacker involved. An outage, a lost key or a ransomware lock denies information to the people entitled to it as completely as theft would.

rows.current: not undertaking the activity that gives rise to the risk
rows.proposed: The only option that removes a risk rather than shrinking it, and the only one that gives up the activity's benefit as well. That trade is why it is rarely as cheap as it looks.

rows.why_selected: leak fire 0.800 against ISO/IEC 27002; also among the shortest at 34 chars
rows.proposed: Both halves matter and the second is where implementations fail. Choosing an algorithm is easy; key custody, rotation and recovery decide whether the protection actually holds.

rows.why_selected: shortest description in the corpus at 28 chars
rows.proposed: Where control passes to walls, doors and locks rather than to configuration. A perimeter drawn on a floor plan is only real if it matches where information is actually handled.

rows.current: a failure to meet a requirement
rows.proposed: Three things have to hold together: a requirement exists, the evidence relates to that requirement, and it shows the requirement unmet. Miss any one and the finding is an observation.
Splits a task so no one person can both act and approve their own action. The aim is removing the opportunity, which is why it applies to trusted people exactly as much as to anyone else.

rows.why_selected: 32 chars; one of the four treatment options
rows.proposed: A decision, not an omission. Retention means someone with the authority to accept it looked at the risk and judged it tolerable against stated criteria; anything else is a risk nobody treated.
Read afterwards as the promise of what the certificate covers, so whatever it leaves ambiguous is resolved against the organization. Interfaces and dependencies are where it usually fails.
What remains once the controls work as intended, which is not the same as what remains because they were never finished. The risk owner has to accept it explicitly before treatment is done.

rows.current: using incidents to improve the ISMS
rows.proposed: The step that turns an incident from a pure cost into information. Skipped, the organization pays for the same failure twice, and clause 10 reads the omission as a gap in improvement.
Minimum for the work being done now, which makes it a review obligation rather than a joining-day one. Access that was correct at hire is usually wrong after the first role change.
Aimed at the visitor, the contractor and the person walking past rather than at a determined attacker, which is why it reaches home and shared workspaces and not only an office floor.
Clause 5.2 asks three separate things: documented, communicated inside the organization, and available to interested parties where appropriate. Publishing a file satisfies only the first.
Asks whether the cause has stopped producing the failure, which needs enough elapsed time or volume to show. Closing a finding the day the fix ships proves only that it was applied.

rows.current: matching treatment effort to risk level
rows.proposed: Cuts both ways. Over-treating a minor risk spends the effort a serious one needed, so this defends the credibility of the assessment and is not merely a way of controlling cost.

rows.current: a weakness that can be exploited by a threat
rows.proposed: Usually the half of a risk you can actually change. The threat rarely goes away, so treatment almost always works by closing or narrowing the weakness it would have to use.
